question: ‘Kim’, the English novel about a boy, was written by which of the following authors?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rudyard Kipling**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kim** is a novel by **Rudyard Kipling**, first published in book form in 1901.
 
• The novel is set against the backdrop of the Great Game, the political conflict between Russia and Britain in Central Asia.
 
• Rudyard Kipling was an English journalist, short-story writer, poet, and novelist.
 
• He is best known for his works of fiction such as "The Jungle Book" and "Kim".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Great Game**:

 
 
• A political and diplomatic confrontation between the British Empire and the Russian Empire.
 
• It took place during the 19th century and early 20th century.
 
• The rivalry was centered on Afghanistan and surrounding regions of Central and South Asia.
 
 
 
• **Rudyard Kipling**:
 
 
• Born on December 30, 1865, in Bombay, British India (now Mumbai, India).
 
• He received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1907.
 
• His other famous works include "The Man Who Would Be King" and "If—".
 
 
 
• **Kim**:
 
 
• The novel explores themes such as British colonialism, espionage, and the clash of cultures.
 
• The protagonist, Kimball O'Hara, is an orphaned boy who grows up on the streets of British India.
 
• Kim becomes involved in espionage as a spy for the British Secret Service.
